history.titleZh: 片上监测器检测AI加速器中的比特翻转攻击（佛罗里达大学、德克萨斯大学达拉斯分校、伦斯勒理工学院）
history.descriptionZh:
佛罗里达大学、德克萨斯大学达拉斯分校和伦斯勒理工学院的研究人员发布技术论文《BARE-AI: Bit-Flip Attack Resilience in AI Hardware through Built-in Performance Monitors》，Semiconductor Engineering以“On-Chip Monitors Detect Bit-Flip Attacks in AI Accelerators”为题进行了报道。该研究关注深度神经网络在安全关键系统中的硬件安全脆弱性。DNN已广泛用于自动驾驶、医疗诊断、航空航天、工业控制等场景，但其权重、偏置、激活值和控制数据通常存储在SRAM/DRAM中，容易受到位翻转攻击（BFA）。攻击者可通过Rowhammer、电压/时钟毛刺、激光故障注入或恶意软件等方式翻转单个或多个比特，篡改模型参数或中间数据，导致推理结果错误、漏检或危险决策，而正常输入下系统可能毫无异常，传统软件测试难以发现。

BARE-AI的核心思想是复用AI加速器已有的内置性能监视器或片上性能计数器，而不是增加专用检测电路。位翻转会改变数据值、激活稀疏性、数据依赖分支、内存访问局部性、缓存命中、DRAM带宽、计算单元利用率和执行时间等微架构行为，从而在性能计数器中留下异常“指纹”。BARE-AI先在无攻击时建立正常推理的性能基线，再在运行时实时采集片上监控数据，通过轻量统计方法或机器学习分类器判断当前推理是否受到位翻转攻击影响。一旦检测到异常，可触发重算、回滚、隔离故障模块、报警或重新加载模型参数，从而将检测能力转化为系统韧性。

该工作的创新点主要包括：第一，将性能监控单元从传统性能与功耗管理扩展到AI硬件安全，提供了一种低面积、低功耗、低侵入的BFA检测路径；第二，不需要修改DNN模型或加速器数据通路，适合已有和未来AI芯片；第三，能在推理过程中在线检测，面向边缘和实时安全关键应用；第四，与ECC、校验和、冗余执行等方案互补，可覆盖ECC难以处理的多比特翻转、数据路径故障或恶意故障注入。论文标题显示其目标是“通过内置性能监视器实现AI硬件的位翻转攻击韧性”，因此不仅关注检测，也可能包含检测后的恢复与缓解机制。

性能与对比方面，新闻可见内容仅给出论文题目和摘要节选，未披露具体检测率、误报率、延迟/功耗/面积开销以及对比基线数据。按该方向通常评估，BARE-AI需要证明在不同DNN、不同AI加速器和不同攻击强度下，能以较低监控开销实现高检测精度，并优于或互补于ECC和冗余方案。其潜在限制是：若位翻转未引起可观测性能变化，或攻击者刻意规避性能指纹，检测可能失效；性能计数器的可用性、采样粒度和虚拟化环境也会影响部署效果。

应用上，该技术可服务于自动驾驶感知、医疗AI、无人机、机器人、工业控制和云端AI加速器等对可靠性与安全性要求高的场景，也可为AI芯片设计提供新思路：在PMU中增加安全相关事件，把运行时性能监控作为硬件安全防线的一部分。总体而言，BARE-AI代表了利用现有片上基础设施实现低成本AI硬件安全监控的趋势，但完整效果仍需论文全文中的实验数据验证。

history.title: Intel's Crescent Island AI accelerator officially powers new GPU D-Series products
history.description: Intel's Crescent Island AI inference accelerator will come to market as the GPU D-Series family, promising 1.3 PFLOPS of FP8 compute alongside up to 480 GB of LPDDR5X delivering 1.5 TB/s of memory bandwidth.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 2 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter At OCP 2026 today, Intel has given Crescent Island a proper name: the Intel GPU D-Series. For the first time, the company also shared a theoretical peak performance target for the chip: 1.3 PFLOPS of FP8. It also disclosed the final memory bandwidth to expect from these AI inference accelerators: 1.5 TB/s. This new information adds to the slow drip of disclosures Intel has made about Crescent Island throughout 2026.We already knew that Crescent Island is the first chip to be built on Intel's Xe3P graphics architecture (or massively parallel computing architecture, really, as the chip lacks most or all of the graphics-specific functional units that would characterize a true GPU). Intel will release GPU D-Series products in an air-cooled PCIe form factor with a TDP of 350W and up to 480GB of LPDDR5X memory.For reference, each of the 72 Rubin GPUs in Nvidia's Vera Rubin NVL72 rack-scale system can push a theoretical 17.5 PFLOPS of FP8 throughput, but each of those chips requires liquid cooling and likely has a TGP measured in kilowatts. In any event, it should be clear that the GPU D-Series is targeting an entirely different performance envelope and infrastructure requirements than Rubin.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Intel GPU D-Series products, in contrast, are meant to be deployed in traditional air-cooled rack servers scaling up to eight GPUs, like Nvidia's HGX systems. In such a configuration, Intel says that GPU D-Series chips could power inference on models spanning more than one trillion parameters. Intel also highlights the chip’s suitability for “large language models, long-context inference, and concurrent inference services," creating a foundation for "multi-tenant AI services, robotics, and other latency-sensitive workloads."In order for that kind of distributed inference deployment to work, in which multiple GPUs will presumably act as one, Intel will also need a robust software stack. The company is highlighting the “common Xe software foundation” it’s already built for AI across its Xe Cores in iGPUs and discrete GPU products. You may like Hot Chips 2026: Intel dives deep on Crescent Island AI accelerator AMD takes the wraps off its Instinct MI455X AI accelerator Hot Chips 2026: Intel Xeon 7 'Diamond Rapids' comes with up to 256 P-cores, 1.28 GB of last-level cache To bring Xe accelerators into the data center, Intel says it’s working with “a broad ecosystem of OEMs, ODMs, neoclouds, independent software vendors, appliance providers, and AI-native companies.” To that end, Intel says customer sampling of GPU D-Series products is in progress, although it didn’t provide any details of a broad launch.It’ll remain to be seen whether the Intel GPU D-Series is the product that finally gives Intel an AI accelerator toehold after the failure of the Data Center GPU Max family (code-named Ponte Vecchio) and its mothballed follow-ons, as well as a series of silicon acquisitions that failed to coalesce into a coherent AI strategy.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsorsBut in a world that’s hungry for every compute cycle for inference, a product with a proven architectural shape that’s targeted specifically at that workload in an accessible thermal and electrical envelope might be just the recipe Intel needs to start getting traction as AI models keep advancing in intelligence and agentic workflows assume ever-greater importance in the computing vision of the future. history.titleZh: Intel的Crescent Island AI加速器正式为全新GPU D系列产品提供动力
history.descriptionZh:
在 OCP 2026 大会上，英特尔正式将此前代号 Crescent Island 的 AI 加速器命名为 Intel GPU D-Series（英特尔 GPU D 系列），并首次公布其理论峰值性能目标：FP8 精度下 1.3 PFLOPS，以及最终内存带宽 1.5 TB/s。这一披露延续了英特尔在 2026 年对该芯片逐步放料的节奏。此前已知，Crescent Island 是首款基于英特尔 Xe3P 图形架构的芯片；但更准确地说，它是一种大规模并行计算架构，因为该芯片缺少或几乎没有真正 GPU 所具备的图形专用功能单元。产品方面，英特尔将推出采用风冷 PCIe 形态的 GPU D-Series，TDP 为 350W，最高配备 480GB LPDDR5X 内存。

作为参照，英伟达 Vera Rubin NVL72 机架级系统中的 72 颗 Rubin GPU，每颗理论 FP8 吞吐可达 17.5 PFLOPS，但每颗都需要液冷，TGP 可能以千瓦计。因此，GPU D-Series 与 Rubin 面向完全不同的性能区间和基础设施要求，不应简单直接对比。D-Series 的定位是部署在传统风冷机架服务器中，最多可扩展至 8 颗 GPU，类似英伟达 HGX 系统。英特尔称，在这种配置下，GPU D-Series 可为参数量超过 1 万亿的模型提供推理能力，并强调其适合“大语言模型、长上下文推理和并发推理服务”，为“多租户 AI 服务、机器人以及其他延迟敏感型工作负载”奠定基础。

要让多颗 GPU 在分布式推理中协同工作、仿佛一颗芯片，英特尔还需要强大的软件栈。公司强调其已为 AI 构建的“通用 Xe 软件基础”，覆盖集成显卡和独立显卡产品中的 Xe 核心。为把 Xe 加速器带入数据中心，英特尔表示正与广泛的生态系统合作，包括 OEM、ODM、新型云服务商、独立软件供应商、设备提供商和 AI 原生公司。目前 GPU D-Series 已进入客户送样阶段，但英特尔未透露大规模上市的具体细节。

该产品能否让英特尔在 AI 加速器市场真正站稳脚跟仍有待观察。此前，英特尔数据中心 GPU Max 系列（代号 Ponte Vecchio）失败，后续产品被搁置，一系列芯片收购也未能整合成连贯的 AI 战略。但在推理算力极度稀缺、AI 模型智能持续提升、代理式工作流日益重要的背景下，一款架构形态经过验证、专门面向推理负载、且热功耗和供电要求相对可接受的产品，或许正是英特尔开始获得市场牵引力所需的配方。

history.title: Meet the modders porting ringfenced DLSS features to older GPUs
history.description: DLSS Multi-Frame Generation and DLSS 5 Neural Rendering can now run on hardware never intended for it, at least according to Nvidia. Now, two of the modders foundational to the release of these community advancements speak out.
history.content: Share Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Over recent weeks, we've seen the release of DLSS 5 Neural Rendering in NBA 2K27, followed by its porting to older GPU generations, and the unlocking of DLSS Multi Frame Generation (MFG) for older graphics cards. But how did all of that happen, and who are the people in the modding community unlocking features that Nvidia itself has locked off from users of anything but its latest Blackwell-based GPUs? We sit down with modders Dashdogy and Uncle Burrito to understand how, and why, the modding community has been breaking down Nvidia's software-based locks.In 2025, during the release of the RTX 5000 series graphics cards, one Australian student was watching a Digital Foundry interview with Nvidia engineers, where the team was showing off Multi Frame Generation (MFG), a feature locked to Blackwell GPUs. During the podcast, the idea of MFG running on older RTX 4000 series hardware was floated, but the feature was never released for Ada Lovelace hardware. “Every few months, I would do a Google search to see if it ever happened or not,” said Dashdogy, a Physics Major studying Mathematics and Space Science.“A few weeks ago now, the perfect storm arrived. Mid-semester break had just started, and I did the same Google search as I always do. But thought, maybe I’ll look into it. How hard could it be?”Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: One AWS instance, and a week of late nights later, he unlocked “true” MFG on Ada Lovelace hardware, a feat previously believed to be impossible due to incompatible instructions and a black screen that blocked the progress of modders before them. We’ve tested the mod extensively, and the results stand out. Multi Frame Generation has unofficially arrived for non-Blackwell hardware.Dashdogy isn’t the only modder that’s been hard at work unlocking features for older-gen GPUs. Several weeks ago, when DLSS5’s Neural Rendering DLL first found its way onto the internet, RTX Remix modder Uncle Burrito set their sights directly on it. “I had no idea of telling [if running DLSS 5 on Ada] was even possible,” they said. Given the previous performance claims of requiring multiple RTX 5090s to run on its initial reveal, Uncle Burrito knew DLSS 5 would be computationally expensive, but that didn’t stop him from trying to get into the DLL itself. You may like Nvidia app update fails to block unofficial DLSS multi-frame generation mod on RTX 40 series gaming GPUs We tested DLSS Multi Frame Generation on RTX 40-series GPUs All-in-one 'DLSS Unlocked' mod brings DLSS 5 and multi-frame gen to RTX 20, 30, and 40 series “Once I reverse-engineered it, with the help of Claude, it became obvious that this was possible on Ada. Not only was most of the code compatible, but to me, it looks like Ada support was simply left behind as a work in progress, not as a hard limit.”And so, less than a day after the DLL had been released in an early access version of NBA 2K27, Uncle Burrito had successfully ported the technology to Ada hardware. In the weeks since the release of Uncle Burrito’s initial unlock for DLSS 5 NR on Ada GPUs, Nvidia has clarified that Neural Rendering would indeed be supported by RTX 4000 series GPUs, lending credence to the idea that implementation on Ada GPUs was merely unfinished in the initial shipping versions of the DLSS 5 DLL.These two foundational mods by Dashdogy and Uncle Burrito now serve as the baseline for endless numbers of forks and integrations of both Neural Rendering and MFG for older hardware, which have now allowed for ports all the way back to 2018’s Turing architecture, and in DLSS 5 NR’s case, ports to AMD hardware. It’s now as simple as using one of many tools to click-and-install both into hundreds of games.Unlocking MFG (Dashdogy) (Image credit: Nvidia)Dashdogy’s experience in modding spans years, having created Stellaris mods while still in High School, making compatibility scripts to patch multiple mods together. But porting DLSS MFG to Ada devices was a different beast entirely. Blackwell and Ada use entirely different ISAs, despite their software similarities. “When this [running Blackwell instructions on Ada] happens, the frames will generate, but the GPU graphs an error and returns a black screen,” he explains.Underpinning Nvidia’s implementations of DLSS in shipping titles are two pieces of software: a package named Streamline, which usually includes a suite of DLSS software, and is a universal translator that allows games to run various upscaling technologies like DLSS. Used in tandem with Streamline is a Neural Graphics Framework (NGX), Nvidia’s proprietary software that underpins its AI-powered efforts like Super Resolution and Frame Generation. As a game calls for tools, NGX cooks the computation, and Streamline serves them to a given game’s engine. What to read next DLSS 5 has already been ported to work on RTX 4000 Series graphics cards Modders bring Nvidia’s DLSS 5 Neural Rendering to AMD Radeon GPUs DLSS 5 mod brings next-gen tech to old Ampere GPUs, but frame rates are horrible As Dashdogy explored how to make MFG compatible with Ada, the modder targeted Streamline and NGX directly. “I specifically spoof the Streamline and NGX calls in memory that define how many frames the GPU is allowed to generate.” This approach allowed an Ada-based GPU to think it was allowed to generate more frames than it ordinarily would. “It’s a pretty simple interception, and on 40-series turns 1 into a 5. Now the GPU knows ‘I am a 4080 and I’m allowed to generate five frames,'" which successfully swerved the black frame issue that other earlier modders encountered, thereby unlocking higher frame generation multipliers.Dashdogy quickly packaged things up as a Cyberpunk 2077 mod, and shipped it off to Nexus Mods. This was the canary in the coal mine for a more mature integration, but things weren’t quite perfect yet. Dashdogy and other modders reported a problem — when using anything more than 2X MFG in Cyberpunk 2077 on Ada, things felt sluggish. Latency wasn’t great, and with the help of another modder, they believed that this was the work of the fabled “Hardware Flip Metering,” which smooths out MFG's outputs, and is a primary reason Nvidia offers as the reason the feature doesn’t work on older graphics cards.Armed with a cloud instance that uses an RTX 6000 Pro Blackwell GPU, Dashdogy quickly went to work improving the MFG mod. “I conducted a kernel dump whilst the GPU was running MFG.” Dashdogy was also equipped with OpenAI’s Daybreak Blue AI model, a modified version of GPT 5.6-Sol with safeguards adjusted to allow for defensive cybersecurity tasks and vulnerability discovery. Using the model and his know-how, he analyzed the RTX 6000 Pro’s kernel dump to check where things might be going wrong for his MFG mod, directly comparing it to his native RTX 4000 Series integration.“For 6X frame generation, the GPU will render two real frames, then generate five frames and place them between those two real frames,” he told Tom’s Hardware Premium. Without copying this integration, frame pacing in his existing solution felt odd and disjointed. "RTX 4080, fix off" shows us a cluster of frames with irregular pacing between raster frame intervals. (Image credit: Dashdogy)“The 40-series-generated frames were all compacted around the middle of the two-frame interval. As you can see [in the image above], what we would expect, and what I measured from the [RTX Pro 6000 Blackwell], was five frames, neatly positioned at separate intervals. However, the 40-series GPU was forcing all of these around the same interval as 2X frame gen would put its one single frame.”This caused the frame pacing of the MFG frames in the initial mod to feel sluggish, weird, and have poor responsiveness, as frame pacing is crucial in making a title feel smooth, especially when any frame generation tool is involved. “I discovered that the 40-series kernel responsible for motion processing was hardcoded to output a midpoint scaling for 2x only,” Dashdogy described. “With multiple generated frames, that compressed their represented motion toward the middle. With the fix, they spread out much more like the Blackwell reference.”“The mod can work anywhere normal frame generation is implemented in any game,” Dashdogy told us, with additional telemetry for users to see exactly what’s changing. “The kernel is the same for both 40-series and 50-series; [it’s] just architecture-specific functionality [which blocks MFG on Ada]. 50-series has a number of Blackwell-specific optimizations that I’ve backported as well, and they contribute to better latency overall.”The modder explains that the frame pacing fix was the most difficult part of the now-universal MFG port to Ada. But after its release, it now sits as a loadable ASI in a game’s directory and controls up to 6X frame generation in supported titles. The project has since been forked by other authors, which plugs the logic Dashdogy wrote into ReShade, a popular graphics mod tool.Unlocking DLSS 5 NR (Uncle Burrito) (Image credit: Remedy Entertainment / Tom's Hardware)“I’ve been working with 3D art and graphics for many years now,” explains Uncle Burrito, a graphics enthusiast who implemented Path Tracing into Need For Speed Underground 2 using RTX Remix several years ago. “Over the years, I’ve stayed in the RTX Remix community to learn a lot more about real-time rendering and the techniques used for it.”After hanging out in Nvidia’s RTX Remix Discord channel, news of the emergence of DLSS 5’s nvngX_dlssnr.dll spread like wildfire. According to Uncle Burrito, mods quickly clamped down on discussion of the DLL, and modders flocked to private channels and alternative servers, such as the RenoDX Discord server, to discuss development and integration. The DLL itself was written specifically for Blackwell, but the Ada architecture shares the ability to read FP8 instructions, which is what the DLL uses to load DLSS 5 Neural Rendering’s model weights.Using that as a starting point, Uncle Burrito quickly went to work. “The model itself is just weights. These weights need code to be executed. The code was only written for Blackwell. CUDA binaries, right?” he explained. But despite this, and the aforementioned difference in ISAs between Blackwell and Ada, certain instructions could not be read by the humbler RTX 4000 series GPUs.“Four of the 15 CUDA binaries [contained within nvngx_dlssnr.dll] would not run on Ada.” But this wasn’t an impossible task, as Uncle Burrito previously explained. The integration for Ada appeared unfinished and therefore, not entirely impossible. “I simply needed to patch the replacement compiled binaries”, meaning that it only took patching four affected CUDA binaries to get things up and running for RTX 4000 series graphics cards, Uncle Burrito told Tom’s Hardware Premium.Uncle Burrito, alongside Ghidra, a reverse engineering tool, and an instance of Claude Code, set out to recompile the incompatible binaries to design a patch, but fell into a roadblock made by Claude itself. “I’m not too familiar with reverse engineering myself [...] Claude made the decision to use the incorrect version of the CUDA SDK to compile the replacement [binaries].” And so, the patched DLL ran, but instead output a black screen. “I could see the NR debug banner, and it did affect my framerate, but the output was completely black.”“This is one of the many pitfalls of vibe coding,” Uncle Burrito said. “You can’t make anything good if you don’t understand what you’re working on. Usually, I don’t give the model any room to gaslight or make a wrong decision. If you don’t know what you’re doing, then don’t expect miracles.”After realizing the mistake and recompiling with the correct CUDA SDK, the results were quickly posted to the RenoDX Discord server. “Ada performance is about as good as it can get. It has native FP8 support, so the hardware is doing its best. The rest can be attributed to simply not [having] enough horsepower in the chips.”The simplicity of the patch might appear to be surprising, but the DLL leans on the same information that’s standardized between games and platforms, similar to how Streamline works in most game engines. “Motion vectors and depth buffer are [two] of the few things in graphics programming that we’ve standardized. Almost every modern game produces motion vectors, and rasterization isn’t possible without a depth/z buffer,” Uncle Burrito told us. Therefore, the DLL becomes a drop-in replacement for the officially distributed one, which unlocks the functionality on Ada.Uncle Burrito’s methodologies were since picked up by RenoDX’s ShortFuse, who then worked on porting the DLSS 5 NR DLL to Ampere and Turing generation graphics cards. That porting work is more involved, since it also includes the translation of the model to be read by FP16 instructions. Following the release of Uncle Burrito’s work, a new DLL has emerged, with universal compatibility between Turing, Ampere, and Ada generations.Unblocking the software lockouts (Image credit: Nvidia)Between the MFG unlocker from Dashdogy and the patched Neural Rendering DLL created by Uncle Burrito, the community-made mods both unlock functionality that would not have come to older-generation cards or would have otherwise been added at a later date. According to Dashdogy, “40-series has no excuse” when it comes to support for Multi Frame Generation. “It’s a very small change that allows [the mod] to work,” noting that additional work is being done to recompile things for Turing and Ampere, with the caveat that latency and overheads get higher the further you go back.“It always comes down to performance,” Uncle Burrito said. “It’s fair for [Nvidia] to not include Ada until they can get the optimization part sorted.” The modder further adds that the situation can be read in both ways, as a method for Nvidia to sell more RTX 5000 series graphics cards, and to have more time to optimize Neural Rendering for older RTX 4000 series GPUs.Everyone wants to make the most out of their available hardware, especially at a time when consumer graphics pricing has firmly rocketed past the moon, with RTX 5090 GPUs now approaching north of $9,000. “I personally think [the MFG mod] is really important in the current market,” Dashdogy adds. “... many are just getting priced out of the new generation entirely, so giving people the ability to hang on to their GPUs for a little bit longer is going to help a lot of people stay invigorated and connected to the hobby.”If a single Australian student can unlock DLSS MFG for older GPUs, Nvidia’s claims of hardware exclusivity appear less like a technical limitation and more like artificial lockout. For those unafraid to modify a few simple files within a game, those features are all readily available, albeit unofficially. There’s an irony in how both MFG and Neural Rendering were ported to older GPUs — the development of both mods relied on cutting-edge AI models — powered by the same ecosystem that’s driving Nvidia’s earnings. Now, the very same AI revolution Nvidia champions is being used to tear down its own walled garden.

history.titleZh: 认识一下那些将受限的DLSS功能移植到旧款GPU上的模组制作者
history.descriptionZh:
过去几周，PC 图形 mod 社区接连完成了两件此前被认为几乎不可能的事：把 DLSS 5 Neural Rendering（神经渲染）带到了非 Blackwell 显卡，并解锁了 Nvidia 原本锁定在 RTX 50 系列上的 DLSS Multi Frame Generation（MFG，多帧生成）。据 Tom's Hardware 与两位核心 modder——Dashdogy 和 Uncle Burrito——的对话，这些破解并非简单的配置文件修改，而是深入 Nvidia 的 Streamline、NGX、DLSS DLL 和 CUDA 二进制层面的逆向工程。其结果不仅让 RTX 40 系 Ada 显卡重新获得新功能，还通过社区 fork 一路扩展到 2018 年的 Turing 架构，甚至把 DLSS 5 神经渲染移植到了 AMD Radeon GPU 上。

背景要从 2025 年 RTX 5000 系列发布说起。当时 Nvidia 工程师在 Digital Foundry 采访中展示了 MFG，并明确将其作为 Blackwell 独占功能。采访中曾有人提出 MFG 是否可能运行在 RTX 40 系 Ada 硬件上，但 Nvidia 从未发布对应支持。澳大利亚物理专业学生 Dashdogy 每隔几个月就搜索一次相关进展。直到最近期中假期开始，他决定亲自研究，最终用一个 AWS 云实例和一周熬夜，在 Ada 显卡上解锁了“真正”的 MFG。此前其他 modder 因指令不兼容和黑屏问题受阻，而 Dashdogy 的成果经 Tom's Hardware 测试后被认为确实有效，意味着 MFG 已非官方地来到非 Blackwell 硬件。

与此同时，RTX Remix 社区 modder Uncle Burrito 盯上了 DLSS 5 神经渲染。他曾在《Need for Speed Underground 2》中用 RTX Remix 实现路径追踪，对实时渲染技术非常熟悉。当 DLSS 5 的 Neural Rendering DLL 首次随《NBA 2K27》早期版本流入互联网后，mod 社区迅速转入私密频道讨论。Uncle Burrito 借助 Claude 进行逆向工程，发现 Ada 架构其实并非完全无法运行：大部分代码兼容，Ada 支持更像是 Nvidia 留下的“未完成工作”，而不是硬性限制。结果在 DLL 泄露不到一天后，他就成功把 DLSS 5 神经渲染移植到了 Ada 硬件。Nvidia 随后也澄清 RTX 4000 系确实会支持神经渲染，这进一步说明早期 DLL 中的 Ada 实现可能只是未完成。

MFG 解锁的核心技术难点在于 Blackwell 与 Ada 使用了不同的 ISA（指令集架构），尽管软件层面相似。Dashdogy 解释，如果直接在 Ada 上运行 Blackwell 指令，帧虽然会生成，但 GPU 会报错并返回黑屏。Nvidia 的 DLSS 实现依赖两个关键组件：Streamline 和 NGX。Streamline 是通用翻译层，让游戏接入 DLSS 等超分辨率技术；NGX 则是 Nvidia 的神经图形框架，负责 AI 超分和帧生成的计算。游戏调用工具时，NGX 负责计算，Streamline 把结果交给游戏引擎。Dashdogy 直接针对 Streamline 和 NGX 的内存调用进行 spoof/拦截，修改 GPU 被允许生成多少帧的定义。这个拦截本身很简单，在 40 系上把“允许生成 1 帧”变成“允许生成 5 帧”，让 GPU 以为“我是一块 4080，我被允许生成五帧”，从而绕开黑屏问题，解锁更高的帧生成倍率。他把成果打包成《赛博朋克 2077》mod 并上传到 Nexus Mods。

但初版并不完美。在 Ada 上使用超过 2X MFG 时，画面会感觉迟钝、延迟不佳、响应差。Dashdogy 认为问题出在 Nvidia 所称的“Hardware Flip Metering”——这是平滑 MFG 输出、也是 Nvidia 声称旧卡不支持 MFG 的主要原因之一。为了修复，他使用搭载 RTX 6000 Pro Blackwell GPU 的云实例，在 GPU 运行 MFG 时进行 kernel dump，并借助 OpenAI 的 Daybreak Blue AI 模型——一个调整了安全限制、可用于防御性网络安全和漏洞发现的 GPT 5.6-Sol 修改版——分析 Blackwell 内核，与 RTX 40 系原生集成对比。

对比发现了关键差异：在 6X 帧生成中，GPU 会渲染两个真实帧，然后生成五个帧并放在这两个真实帧之间。Dashdogy 测得 RTX 6000 Pro Blackwell 会把五个生成帧均匀分布在多个间隔上；但 40 系 GPU 却把生成帧全部挤在两个真实帧的中间区间，类似 2X 帧生成只放一帧时的行为。这是因为 40 系负责运动处理的内核被硬编码为只输出 2X 的中点缩放，多个生成帧的运动信息因此被压缩到中间，导致帧节奏怪异、迟钝。修复后，生成帧的分布更接近 Blackwell 参考。该 mod 可作为游戏目录中的 ASI 加载，在支持的游戏中控制最高 6X 帧生成，并加入遥测信息供用户观察变化。Dashdogy 还指出，40 系和 50 系内核相同，真正阻止 Ada 的是架构特定功能；他还把多项 Blackwell 专属优化回移到 40 系，改善了整体延迟。该逻辑后来被 fork 进 ReShade。

DLSS 5 神经渲染的移植则由 Uncle Burrito 完成。DLSS 5 的 nvngx_dlssnr.dll 专为 Blackwell 编写，但 Ada 同样支持 FP8 指令，而 DLL 正是用 FP8 加载神经渲染的模型权重。不过模型权重只是数据，执行还需要代码，也就是 CUDA 二进制。Uncle Burrito 发现，DLL 内含 15 个 CUDA 二进制，其中 4 个无法在 Ada 上运行。由于 Ada 集成看起来只是未完成，而非绝对不可能，他只需修补并替换这 4 个受影响的编译二进制。他使用逆向工具 Ghidra 和 Claude Code 尝试重新编译，但 Claude 选择了错误的 CUDA SDK 版本，导致补丁 DLL 虽然能运行、能看到 NR 调试横幅、也会影响帧率，但输出完全是黑屏。Uncle Burrito 称这是“vibe coding”的典型陷阱：如果不理解自己在做什么，就不能期待奇迹。改用正确 CUDA SDK 重新编译后，补丁成功，并被发到 RenoDX Discord。

性能方面，Uncle Burrito 表示 Ada 表现“已经接近能到的最好水平”，因为 Ada 原生支持 FP8，硬件已经尽力，剩余差距主要来自芯片算力不足。这个补丁之所以相对简单，是因为 DLL 依赖游戏和平台之间已经标准化的信息，例如运动矢量和深度缓冲。几乎所有现代游戏都会生成运动矢量，光栅化也离不开深度/Z 缓冲，因此该 DLL 可以作为官方 DLL 的直接替代品，在 Ada 上解锁功能。此后，RenoDX 的 ShortFuse 接手，把 DLSS 5 神经渲染 DLL 进一步移植到 Ampere 和 Turing。由于需要把模型转换为 FP16 指令可读取的格式，这一过程更复杂。最终出现了可在 Turing、Ampere 和 Ada 之间通用兼容的新 DLL。

这些社区 mod 的意义不只是“让老卡跑新功能”。Dashdogy 认为，RTX 40 系“没有任何借口”不支持 MFG，因为改动非常小；目前还有工作在为 Turing 和 Ampere 重新编译，但显卡越老，延迟和开销越高。Uncle Burrito 则指出，一切最终都取决于性能。Nvidia 在优化完成前不把 Ada 纳入支持，从商业角度有其合理性；但这件事也可以从另一面看：既是为了推动 RTX 5000 系列销售，也是为了给自己争取更多时间，为 RTX 4000 系优化神经渲染。在当前显卡价格飞涨、RTX 5090 已接近 9000 美元的市场上，Dashdogy 认为 MFG mod 非常重要，因为很多人已经被新一代显卡的价格排除在外，能让用户多撑一段时间，有助于他们继续留在 PC 硬件爱好中。

更具讽刺意味的是，这两个解锁旧 GPU 功能的 mod，都依赖最前沿的 AI 模型来完成逆向工程和代码分析，而这些 AI 生态恰恰也是推动 Nvidia 业绩增长的重要力量。如今，Nvidia 所倡导的 AI 革命，正在被社区用来拆掉它自己筑起的硬件围墙。如果一个澳大利亚学生就能为旧 GPU 解锁 DLSS MFG，那么 Nvidia 所宣称的硬件独占，看起来就不再像纯粹的技术限制，而更像人为锁区。对于不怕修改几个游戏文件的用户来说，这些功能已经可以非官方地使用。

history.content: As AI factories grow from megawatts to gigawatts, building them takes more than advanced computing. Open standards are helping the industry scale AI infrastructure faster, more efficiently and more reliably. At the Open Compute Project (OCP) Global Summit, taking place in the San Jose McEnery Convention Center, NVIDIA announced new partnerships and contributions aimed at creating a common foundation for next-generation AI infrastructure. NVIDIA contributed key NVIDIA Vera Rubin rack and compute tray designs to OCP through the open NVIDIA MGX architecture, giving system builders a common foundation for developing next-generation AI factory infrastructure. Together, these efforts span the AI factory itself, the utility grid that powers it and the rack-scale architecture at the heart of modern accelerated computing. NVIDIA and Partners Announce Open Architecture Advances At the OCP event, NVIDIA and partners made a handful of announcements: NVIDIA and hyperscalers published open standards for next-generation AI factories, including AI factory design standards and grid resilience. NVIDIA launched new open source software components for NVIDIA DSX AI Factory. Meta and NVIDIA advanced open AI networking with NVIDIA Spectrum-X Ethernet SuperNIC and Spectrum-6 innovations. Visionbay introduced an 800V DC AI factory design for the Vera Rubin era. NVIDIA and Cisco announced the Ultra-Dense Small Form Factor Pluggable (USFP) standard, the industry’s first module ​for 400Gb/s-based networking fabrics. NVIDIA and Google announced Falcon Transport support on future NVIDIA ConnectX-10 SuperNICs and BlueField DPUs. Before a packed audience, Ian Buck, vice president of hyperscale and high-performance computing at NVIDIA, discussed how open infrastructure is becoming a critical ingredient for scaling AI factories worldwide. The news at OCP spotlights how NVIDIA’s extreme codesign combined with open standards is accelerating deployment, improving power efficiency and driving tokens-per-watt performance. Vera Rubin AI Factories Advance With MGX Rack Contributions at OCP 🔗 NVIDIA joined industry leaders in contributing to the third-generation MGX AI data center reference design through OCP’s Open DC Initiative. Combined with open liquid-cooling technologies such as MQD and MQDB, the effort helps turn proven AI factory designs into industry standards that others can adopt, manufacture and scale. For NVIDIA Vera Rubin AI factories, the updated MGX 1.2 specification extends the open architecture for AI factories with rack-scale blind-mate liquid cooling, interoperable rack-scale interconnect infrastructure and a liquid-cooled 5,000A busbar designed for higher-power AI systems. It also adds native 19-inch equipment support and higher-density rack designs. MGX 1.2 further expands modularity with configurable I/O bays, fanless liquid-cooled compute trays, standardized power and cooling interfaces, and a common infrastructure that helps ecosystem partners build interoperable accelerated computing platforms. It improves assembly, test and service times to streamline manufacturing and field service to enable faster and more efficient infrastructure buildout. The architecture supports rack deployments up to 250kW while simplifying serviceability, deployment and infrastructure reuse. The Vera CPU rack design specification extends the NVIDIA MGX open architecture beyond accelerated computing, providing a purpose-built platform for the growing agentic AI era. While Vera Rubin NVL72 serves as the foundation for large-scale training and inference, the NVIDIA Vera CPU rack is designed to support tool calling, orchestration and sandboxed execution, helping AI agents interact with applications, data and services in real time. Built on the third-generation NVIDIA MGX rack architecture, the Vera CPU rack shares the same rack-scale design principles that unite compute, networking, power and cooling into a common modular platform. This approach enables partners to deploy specialized infrastructure while benefiting from a shared ecosystem, simplified integration and a consistent foundation for next-generation AI factories. NVIDIA Launches New Open Source Software Components for DSX AI Factory 🔗 NVIDIA DSX AI factory platform applies extreme codesign to unify computing, networking, power, cooling, facilities and software, helping AI factories operate as a single optimized system, maximizing AI output within available infrastructure constraints. At the center of this unified system is DSX OS, the open operating layer that turns the DSX architecture into coordinated, repeatable operations at scale. At OCP, NVIDIA expanded DSX OS with open source components for configuring networks, validating clusters, managing racks and provisioning bare metal: NVIDIA Config Manager: Automates switch configurations at scale, allowing customers to deploy, validate and maintain consistent AI factory network fabrics with minimal to zero manual intervention/ NVIDIA Cluster Readiness Engine: Helps eliminate costly job crashes by stress-testing GPU clusters with real workload simulations to guarantee hardware health before training begins NVIDIA Rack Management Service: Offers a rack hardware abstraction and operations solutions that treats racks as first-class units for improved AI factory scale firmware management. Cluster API Provider for NVIDIA Infrastructure Controller: Accelerates bare-metal deployment and tenant onboarding, turning raw AI hardware into production-ready clusters in hours instead of days. Developed from NVIDIA’s experience running NVIDIA DGX Cloud, these open source components enable cloud providers and software partners to integrate AI factory capabilities directly into their multi-tenant platforms. Developers can visit the DSX AI Factory Github page to explore and contribute to both the new and existing open source software components from NVIDIA DSX AI Factory platform. NVIDIA and Hyperscalers Publish Open Standards for Next-Generation AI Factories 🔗 For AI infrastructure to scale globally, it needs more than advanced hardware — it needs a common foundation that the entire industry can build on. At OCP, NVIDIA joined AMD, Google and Meta to publish a new open specification that establishes that foundation. The Open Data Center Specification v0.7 defines a unified blueprint for next-generation AI factory facility design — from power architecture to cooling infrastructure to physical layout. The OCP Grid Resilience Specification, published by Google, Meta, Microsoft and NVIDIA, establishes how large-scale AI infrastructure should behave during utility grid disturbances: staying connected, responding automatically and restoring to near-full load within less than two seconds. With these standards now open, manufacturers around the world have a common target to build for. Equipment makers, colocation providers and data center operators can begin designing, fabricating and delivering the infrastructure layer that powers AI factories under construction globally — without waiting for proprietary specifications from individual customers. Being NVIDIA DSX reference design-compatible, these specifications provide a validated, deployable implementation of both specs, from facility layout and power architecture to the software that monitors and responds to grid signals in real time. For operators building Vera Rubin AI factories, there’s now a straight line from open community standard to a running system. Visionbay.ai Designs 800VDC AI Factory for the Vera Rubin Era 🔗 As AI factories grow larger and more powerful, one challenge looms over them all: delivering enough power to the accelerated computing systems driving the next generation of AI. At OCP, Visionbay unveiled plans for K-1, a next-generation AI factory platform designed around an 800 VDC architecture and built with future NVIDIA Vera Rubin deployments in mind. The project combines NVIDIA’s 800 VDC reference architecture with power and thermal technologies from Vertiv to create a scalable foundation for high-density AI infrastructure. The design addresses a growing industry challenge. As AI training, inference and reasoning workloads expand, rack power densities continue to rise. Traditional low-voltage power distribution becomes increasingly difficult to scale, requiring more copper, more cabling and more power-conversion equipment. By adopting NVIDIA’s 800 VDC architecture, K-1 creates a path toward higher-density AI infrastructure while preserving flexibility for existing deployments. Rather than requiring a complete transition on day one, the platform is designed to phase in 800 VDC distribution where it delivers the greatest benefit, helping operators prepare for future generations of accelerated computing without extensive facility redesign. The architecture is designed around cluster-level power centers that centralize AC-to-DC conversion and distribute 800 VDC closer to compute resources. The approach simplifies downstream power delivery, supports modular expansion and creates repeatable building blocks for future AI factory growth. K-1 also reflects the system-level design philosophy behind NVIDIA AI factories, where power, cooling and computing are engineered together. With support for liquid-cooled infrastructure, scalable power distribution and future Vera Rubin-class deployments, the project demonstrates how ecosystem partners are translating NVIDIA’s AI factory architecture into deployable infrastructure designed for the next era of accelerated computing. Meta and NVIDIA Advance AI Networking With Spectrum-6 and Multiplane Technology 🔗 At the event, Meta and NVIDIA announced that Meta is adopting NVIDIA Spectrum-6 102.4Tb/s Ethernet switches to build larger, higher-performance NVIDIA Vera Rubin AI factories on open networking. Spectrum-6 delivers twice the switching capacity and per-lane bandwidth of Spectrum-4, and provides a lossless Ethernet AI fabric at 200G per lane, with high effective bandwidth and performance isolation that keeps one job’s traffic from slowing another’s. Meta’s Spectrum-6-based switch, N-IceCube, slots into IcePack, Meta’s 100T, liquid-cooled rack. N-IceCube runs the Facebook Open Switching System (FBOSS), Meta’s open source network operating system that contributed to OCP to support efficient networking at hyperscale. FBOSS is built on the Switch Abstraction Interface, an OCP standard NVIDIA helped develop, providing a vendor-independent way of controlling switch hardware. Together, these technologies support agentic AI factories of more than 100,000 GPUs that train and serve massive mixture-of-experts models. The announcement marks the next step in a collaboration that combines Meta’s experience operating AI infrastructure at hyperscale with NVIDIA’s networking technology. At the heart of this collaboration is Spectrum-X Multiplane technology, enabled by Spectrum-6 switches and ConnectX-9 SuperNICs. Multiplane distributes GPU traffic in hardware across up to eight independent network planes, enabling AI factories to scale beyond 100,000 GPUs with fewer switch tiers and lower infrastructure costs. Multiple paths between GPUs improve network utilization and resilience: when a component fails, traffic shifts to the remaining planes, keeping GPUs productive and AI applications running, even at reduced bandwidth. Meta and NVIDIA worked together to strengthen that resilience through deployment experience and rapid engineering iteration. The teams validated improvements across on-premises and cloud environments. “We are excited about our close partnership with NVIDIA in making multiplane fabrics operationally scalable and performant, a critical requirement both for our own infrastructure builds and for our joint cloud partners,” said Omar Baldonado, senior director of data center and AI networking at Meta. “Extending FBOSS to Spectrum ASICs means we can run that same software stack across our fabrics, and Meta’s new Spectrum-based switch, N-IceCube, brings that into Icepack – our liquid-cooled 102.4T network rack for scale-out that connects upcoming generations of accelerators in our fleet.” Together, Meta and NVIDIA are developing an architecture and operational playbook that other AI infrastructure operators can adopt, turning lessons from demanding production workloads into more scalable, resilient and efficient AI factories. With USFP, NVIDIA and Cisco Reinvent Pluggable Optics for AI Factory Scale 🔗 As AI factories scale to support larger models and surging inference demand, every component of the infrastructure stack must deliver more performance, efficiency and simplicity — right down to the network connection itself. At OCP, NVIDIA and Cisco announced plans for USFP, a new optical pluggable transceiver module form factor designed to help AI factory builders scale next-generation AI fabrics while improving bandwidth density and power efficiency. With approximately the same footprint as the widely adopted 200Gb/s-per-lane OSFP form factor, USFP will provide a path to 400Gb/s-per-lane networking and will extend a transceiver-based deployment model already proven across generations of data center networks. Packing 16 full-duplex lanes with plans to scale up to 32 lanes, USFP will deliver four times the bandwidth density of traditional 200Gb/s-per-lane pluggable optics. The result is the ability to connect more compute resources without adding network tiers that can increase latency, power consumption and complexity. The new form factor is designed for the scale and efficiency demands of next generation AI factories, supporting higher-bandwidth fabrics while preserving the flexibility and serviceability that have made pluggable optics a mainstay of modern data centers. It also will deliver roughly 1.3x greater power efficiency, helping operators move more data with less energy. To help drive an open ecosystem, NVIDIA and Cisco are collaborating with TE Connectivity and Amphenol on cages, connectors and modules, with plans to advance USFP through a community-led, multi-source effort. Together, the companies are laying the foundation for more scalable, efficient and interoperable AI factory networking. Google Falcon Transport Supports NVIDIA ConnectX-10 for Interoperable AI Networking 🔗 NVIDIA and Google also announced Falcon Transport support on future NVIDIA ConnectX-10 SuperNICs and BlueField DPUs, helping improve network efficiency for large-scale AI infrastructure. Falcon is a transport protocol designed to deliver data reliably over Ethernet networks, which can otherwise drop packets under congestion. It supports AI and storage workloads through multipath load balancing, programmable congestion control, hardware loss recovery and per-connection security. This collaboration combines NVIDIA hardware acceleration with DOCA software to implement Falcon and extend NVIDIA networking to Google’s data center transport. NVIDIA and Google NICs can communicate over a common transport while applications retain standard RDMA programming interfaces. By distributing traffic across paths, adapting to congestion, recovering dropped packets and protecting connections, Falcon helps workloads make better use of available bandwidth and maintain predictable performance as Ethernet fabrics scale. Learn more by joining NVIDIA at OCP.

history.titleZh: OCP Global Summit: Amid Ecosystem Adoption, NVIDIA Opens Vera Rubin Architecture to Help Scale AI Factories Worldwide
history.descriptionZh:
在圣何塞麦克内里会议中心举行的OCP全球峰会上，NVIDIA宣布了一系列新合作与贡献，目标是为下一代AI基础设施建立共同基础。随着AI工厂从兆瓦级扩展到吉瓦级，建设它们不再只是先进计算的问题，还涉及供电、冷却、网络、机架和软件运营。开放标准正帮助行业更快、更高效、更可靠地扩展AI基础设施。NVIDIA通过开放的MGX架构，向OCP贡献了关键的Vera Rubin机架和计算托盘设计，让系统构建商拥有开发下一代AI工厂基础设施的共同基础。整体来看，这些努力覆盖AI工厂本身、为其供电的公用电网，以及现代加速计算核心的机架级架构。

NVIDIA hyperscale与高性能计算副总裁Ian Buck在座无虚席的观众前表示，开放基础设施正在成为全球扩展AI工厂的关键要素。OCP上的发布显示，NVIDIA的“极致协同设计”与开放标准结合，正在加速部署、提升能效并推动每瓦Token性能。

**MGX与Vera Rubin：机架级开放架构延伸到代理式AI**

NVIDIA与行业领导者一起，通过OCP的Open DC Initiative贡献了第三代MGX AI数据中心参考设计。结合MQD、MQDB等开放液冷技术，这一努力把经过验证的AI工厂设计转化为行业标准，使其他厂商可以采用、制造和扩展。针对NVIDIA Vera Rubin AI工厂，更新的MGX 1.2规范扩展了AI工厂开放架构，引入机架级盲插液冷、可互操作的机架级互连基础设施，以及面向更高功率AI系统的液冷5000A母线。它还增加了对原生19英寸设备的支持，以及更高密度机架设计。

MGX 1.2进一步增强了模块化能力，包括可配置I/O bay、无风扇液冷计算托盘、标准化电源和冷却接口，以及帮助生态伙伴构建可互操作加速计算平台的通用基础设施。该架构改进了组装、测试和服务时间，简化制造与现场服务，从而加快基础设施部署。它支持最高250kW的机架部署，同时简化可维护性、部署和基础设施复用。

Vera CPU机架设计规范则把NVIDIA MGX开放架构扩展到加速计算之外，为不断增长的代理式AI时代提供专用平台。Vera Rubin NVL72面向大规模训练和推理，而NVIDIA Vera CPU机架用于支持工具调用、编排和沙箱化执行，帮助AI代理实时与应用、数据和服务交互。Vera CPU机架基于第三代NVIDIA MGX机架架构，与Vera Rubin共享同一套机架级设计原则，把计算、网络、电源和冷却统一到通用模块化平台中，使伙伴能够部署专用基础设施，同时受益于共享生态、简化集成和一致基础。

**DSX AI Factory：用开源软件统一AI工厂运营**

NVIDIA DSX AI工厂平台通过极致协同设计，统一计算、网络、电源、冷却、设施和软件，使AI工厂作为一个整体优化系统运行，在现有基础设施约束下最大化AI输出。其核心是DSX OS，这一开放操作层把DSX架构转化为可协调、可重复的大规模运营。

在OCP上，NVIDIA扩展了DSX OS，推出多个开源组件：NVIDIA Config Manager可大规模自动化交换机配置，让客户以最少甚至零人工干预部署、验证和维护一致的AI工厂网络结构；NVIDIA Cluster Readiness Engine通过真实工作负载模拟对GPU集群进行压力测试，在训练开始前保证硬件健康，避免代价高昂的作业崩溃；NVIDIA Rack Management Service提供机架硬件抽象和运营方案，把机架作为一等单元，改善AI工厂规模的固件管理；Cluster API Provider for NVIDIA Infrastructure Controller则加速裸金属部署和租户上线，把原始AI硬件变成生产级集群的时间从数天缩短到数小时。这些组件源自NVIDIA运营DGX Cloud的经验，可帮助云提供商和软件伙伴把AI工厂能力直接集成到多租户平台。开发者可在DSX AI Factory GitHub页面探索和贡献新老开源组件。

**开放标准与电网韧性：让全球制造业有共同目标**

AI基础设施要全球扩展，不能只靠先进硬件，还需要全行业可构建的共同基础。在OCP上，NVIDIA与AMD、Google、Meta共同发布了新的开放规范Open Data Center Specification v0.7，为下一代AI工厂设施设计确立统一蓝图，涵盖电源架构、冷却基础设施和物理布局。由Google、Meta、Microsoft和NVIDIA发布的OCP Grid Resilience Specification，则规定大型AI基础设施在公用电网扰动期间应如何表现：保持连接、自动响应，并在不到两秒内恢复到接近满负载。

这些标准开放后，全球制造商有了共同目标。设备制造商、托管提供商和数据中心运营商可以开始设计、制造和交付为全球在建AI工厂供电的基础设施层，而不必等待单个客户的专有规范。由于兼容NVIDIA DSX参考设计，这些规范提供了经过验证、可部署的实现，从设施布局和电源架构，到实时监控和响应电网信号的软件。对于建设Vera Rubin AI工厂的运营商来说，从开放社区标准到运行系统已有清晰路径。

**Visionbay K-1：面向Vera Rubin时代的800VDC AI工厂**

随着AI工厂变得更大更强，一个共同挑战日益突出：如何为驱动下一代AI的加速计算系统提供足够电力。在OCP上，Visionbay公布了K-1计划，这是围绕800VDC架构设计、面向未来NVIDIA Vera Rubin部署的下一代AI工厂平台。该项目结合NVIDIA的800VDC参考架构与Vertiv的电源和热管理技术，为高密度AI基础设施建立可扩展基础。

这一设计针对行业挑战：随着AI训练、推理和推理型工作负载扩大，机架功率密度持续上升，传统低压配电越来越难扩展，需要更多铜、更多线缆和更多电源转换设备。采用NVIDIA 800VDC架构后，K-1为更高密度AI基础设施提供路径，同时保留现有部署灵活性。它不要求第一天就完全转换，而是设计为在收益最大处逐步引入800VDC配电，帮助运营商为未来几代加速计算做准备，而无需大规模改造设施。架构围绕集群级电源中心，集中完成AC-DC转换，并把800VDC分配到更接近计算资源的位置，从而简化下游供电、支持模块化扩展，并形成可重复的AI工厂增长构建块。K-1也体现了NVIDIA AI工厂的系统级设计哲学：电源、冷却和计算一起设计。它支持液冷基础设施、可扩展配电和未来Vera Rubin级部署，展示了生态伙伴如何把NVIDIA AI工厂架构转化为面向下一代加速计算的可部署基础设施。

**Meta与NVIDIA：Spectrum-6和Multiplane推进开放AI网络**

Meta与NVIDIA宣布，Meta将采用NVIDIA Spectrum-6 102.4Tb/s以太网交换机，在开放网络上构建更大、更高性能的NVIDIA Vera Rubin AI工厂。Spectrum-6的交换容量和每通道带宽都是Spectrum-4的两倍，提供每通道200G的无损以太网AI fabric，具备高有效带宽和性能隔离能力，可防止一个作业的流量拖慢另一个作业。Meta基于Spectrum-6的交换机N-IceCube将装入IcePack，即Meta的100T液冷机架。N-IceCube运行Facebook Open Switching System，这是Meta贡献给OCP的开源网络操作系统，用于支持超大规模高效网络。FBOSS建立在Switch Abstraction Interface之上，这是NVIDIA帮助开发的OCP标准，提供厂商无关的交换机硬件控制方式。

这些技术共同支持超过10万GPU的代理式AI工厂，用于训练和提供大规模混合专家模型服务。此次合作结合了Meta在超大规模AI基础设施运营方面的经验与NVIDIA的网络技术。核心是Spectrum-X Multiplane技术，由Spectrum-6交换机和ConnectX-9 SuperNIC支持。Multiplane在硬件中把GPU流量分布到最多8个独立网络平面，使AI工厂能够以更少交换机层级和更低基础设施成本扩展到10万GPU以上。GPU之间的多条路径提高了网络利用率和韧性：当某个组件故障时，流量会转移到剩余平面，即使带宽降低，也能保持GPU生产力和AI应用运行。Meta与NVIDIA通过部署经验和快速工程迭代增强了这种韧性，并在本地和云环境中验证了改进。

Meta数据中心与AI网络高级总监Omar Baldonado表示，与NVIDIA的紧密合作使multiplane fabric在运营上可扩展且高性能，这对Meta自身基础设施和联合云伙伴都是关键需求。把FBOSS扩展到Spectrum ASIC意味着同一软件栈可跨Meta的fabric运行，而新的N-IceCube交换机把这一能力带入IcePack——Meta用于横向扩展的液冷102.4T网络机架，连接未来几代加速器。Meta和NVIDIA正在共同开发其他AI基础设施运营商可采用的架构和运营手册，把严苛生产工作负载的经验转化为更可扩展、更有韧性和更高效的AI工厂。

**USFP：NVIDIA与Cisco重新定义AI工厂规模的可插拔光模块**

随着AI工厂扩展以支持更大模型和激增的推理需求，基础设施栈的每个组件都必须提供更高性能、效率和简单性，网络连接也不例外。在OCP上，NVIDIA与Cisco宣布USFP计划，这是一种新的光学可插拔收发器模块外形，旨在帮助AI工厂建设者扩展下一代AI fabric，同时提高带宽密度和能效。USFP的占板面积与广泛采用的每通道200Gb/s OSFP大致相同，但将提供通往每通道400Gb/s网络的路径，并延续已在多代数据中心网络中验证的收发器部署模式。它封装16个全双工通道，并计划扩展到32通道，提供传统每通道200Gb/s可插拔光模块四倍的带宽密度。这意味着可以连接更多计算资源，而无需增加会提高延迟、功耗和复杂度的网络层级。

新外形面向下一代AI工厂的规模和效率需求，支持更高带宽fabric，同时保留使可插拔光模块成为现代数据中心主力的灵活性和可维护性。它还将带来约1.3倍的能效提升，帮助运营商用更少能源传输更多数据。为推动开放生态，NVIDIA和Cisco正与TE Connectivity和Amphenol合作开发笼子、连接器和模块，并计划通过社区主导、多来源方式推进USFP。这些公司正在为更可扩展、高效和可互操作的AI工厂网络奠定基础。

**Google Falcon Transport支持NVIDIA ConnectX-10，实现可互操作AI网络**

NVIDIA与Google还宣布，未来NVIDIA ConnectX-10 SuperNIC和BlueField DPU将支持Falcon Transport，以提高大规模AI基础设施的网络效率。Falcon是一种传输协议，用于在以太网上可靠传输数据，而以太网在拥塞时可能会丢包。它通过多路径负载均衡、可编程拥塞控制、硬件丢包恢复和每连接安全来支持AI和存储工作负载。此次合作把NVIDIA硬件加速与DOCA软件结合，实现Falcon，并把NVIDIA网络扩展到Google数据中心传输。NVIDIA和Google的网卡可以通过公共传输协议通信，同时应用保留标准RDMA编程接口。通过分散流量、适应拥塞、恢复丢包和保护连接，Falcon帮助工作负载更好地利用可用带宽，并在以太网fabric扩展时保持可预测性能。

整体而言，NVIDIA在OCP上的发布表明，下一代AI工厂的竞争不仅是芯片和服务器之争，更是开放架构、供电、冷却、网络、软件运营和行业标准之争。从MGX机架、DSX OS、800VDC供电，到Spectrum-6、Multiplane、USFP和Falcon Transport，NVIDIA正试图把自身在加速计算、网络和系统级协同设计上的能力，转化为整个生态可采用、可制造、可扩展的开放基础设施基础。这将直接影响超大规模云厂商、设备制造商、数据中心运营商和AI软件伙伴，也为未来十万GPU级甚至更大规模的代理式AI工厂铺路。

history.title: Developer uses Claude to enable Xbox Cloud Gaming on jailbroken PS5s
history.description: RafaelNGP released a native Xbox Game Pass app allowing Xbox Cloud Gaming on the PS5, with support for 4 controllers and 4K upscaling on the PS5 GPU.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 1 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Brazilian developer RafaelNGP has created his own Homebrew called PSBox Cloud Gaming on his jailbroken PS5 and released it for download on GitHub. The mod, created in part using Claude, allows Xbox Cloud Gaming to run natively on a PS5, with up to 4 DualSense controllers mapped to Xbox for compatibility.The lines between consoles and PC have been blurring lately, and even more so for the PS5, with jailbreak mods allowing for many new capabilities it was never intended for. We recently covered a story about the original Xbox being emulated on a jailbroken PS5, but a more modern and usable mod is this natively running Xbox Cloud Gaming mod. Gone are the days of switching to your Xbox or PC to play xCloud; just run it on your PS5 — that's what RafaelNGP thought to himself before making PSBox Cloud Gaming.GitHub - RafaelNGP/xbox-cloud-gaming-ps5: Xbox Cloud Gaming app for PS5 Homebrew from r/PS5_JailbreakRafael explains how easy it is to get it running, with just a .zip file download from their GitHub, extraction to a specific folder, waiting for a Homebrew loader to mount the “game,” then launch and sign in as usual. Users are able to sign in using their phone through a code on the TV. It currently supports a 1080p60 stream, but can be upscaled to 4K using the PS5’s GPU with AMD FSR 1 or Anime4K upscalers. The application is still not perfect, with testers reporting video issues such as macroblocking, pink artifacts, and vibration issues on the DualSense controllers, while others are thrilled and having a good experience.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: As if emulating the original Xbox and playing xCloud on a PS5 weren’t enough, a comment under the Reddit post asked whether they could use local Xbox Remote Play on it, intending to stream games from an Xbox they already have to the PS5. Rafael said it didn’t work yet, but promptly created an update days later enabling Xbox Remote Play.The PS5’s library of exclusives may be lackluster, but it seems that the PS5 has more to offer than its own games outside of what Sony intends for it, thanks to the jailbreaking community. history.titleZh: 开发者利用Claude在已越狱的PS5上实现Xbox云游戏
history.descriptionZh:
巴西开发者 RafaelNGP 在越狱 PS5 上制作了一款名为 PSBox Cloud Gaming 的 Homebrew 应用，并在 GitHub 上发布供下载。该项目部分借助 Claude 完成，核心功能是让 Xbox Cloud Gaming 在 PS5 上原生运行，并最多支持 4 个 DualSense 控制器映射为 Xbox 控制器以实现兼容。其背景是主机与 PC 的界限日益模糊，PS5 越狱社区不断解锁索尼原本未开放的能力；此前已有越狱 PS5 模拟初代 Xbox 的案例，而这次的项目更现代、更实用，目标是让玩家不再需要切换到 Xbox 或 PC 就能玩 xCloud。

从技术实现看，PSBox Cloud Gaming 依赖越狱后的 Homebrew 环境，而非索尼官方支持。用户只需从 GitHub 下载 .zip 文件，解压到指定文件夹，等待 Homebrew loader 将应用挂载为“游戏”，然后启动并按常规方式登录。登录时可通过电视上的代码用手机完成。其创新点在于把 Xbox 云游戏客户端和手柄映射带入 PS5，并在 Reddit 用户询问后进一步扩展功能：开发者最初表示本地 Xbox Remote Play 尚不可用，但几天后便发布更新，加入了对 Xbox Remote Play 的支持，使 PS5 可以串流玩家已有 Xbox 上的游戏。

性能方面，该应用目前支持 1080p60 串流，并可利用 PS5 GPU 配合 AMD FSR 1 或 Anime4K 上采样器提升到 4K。不过它仍不完美，测试者报告了宏块、粉色伪影以及 DualSense 振动问题等视频和手柄问题，但也有用户表示体验良好。与过去必须使用 Xbox 或 PC 才能玩 xCloud 相比，这个 mod 将跨平台云游戏和远程游玩能力带到了 PS5。其影响在于，它扩展了 PS5 的用途，展示了云游戏、远程串流和跨生态手柄映射的可能性，也体现了越狱社区在官方限制之外推动主机功能边界的作用。文章还提及类似越狱项目，例如在 PS5 上运行 Nintendo Switch 游戏、提供原生 PS2 光盘支持和 4K 升频等。

history.title: Intel to phase out SGX after Xeon Diamond Rapids in favor of TDX
history.description: Intel set to discontinue SGX after Xeon 'Diamond Rapids' and focus on expanding TDX capabilities to meet emerging security requirements of cloud computing, enterprise workloads, and agentic AI.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Just five years after bringing its Software Guard Extensions (SGX) technology to its mainstream server platform, Intel on Friday announced plans to discontinue its support after its upcoming Xeon 'Diamond Rapids' CPUs and concentrate its confidential computing efforts on Trust Domain Extensions (TDX). The company will continue to support existing SGX-enabled platforms into the early 2030s, but at the same time will expand TDX capabilities to address emerging requirements of cloud computing, enterprise workloads, and agentic AI applications.Without a doubt, data sovereignty requirements are an increasingly important factor as organizations seek to protect sensitive information from unauthorized access even when they process it on infrastructure operated by third parties. Although both Intel SGX and TDX are designed to protect sensitive information while it is being processed, they use substantially different approaches.SGX provides hardware-protected enclaves within applications to isolate selected code and data from other software, including the operating system and hypervisor. By contrast, TDX isolates entire virtual machines from the underlying host environment, including the hypervisor and other VMs. While SGX requires developers to design or modify applications to use protected enclaves, TDX can protect existing workloads inside confidential VMs without extensive changes to individual applications, something that makes TDX particularly attractive to cloud service providers that operate large numbers of virtual machines.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: While both SGX and TDX have faced numerous security vulnerabilities over the years, including side-channel attacks, privilege-escalation flaws, and attacks against their attestation mechanisms, Intel does not cite security concerns as a reason for its decision to discontinue SGX.Intel's decision to phase out SGX reflects the industry's preference for VM-level isolation over application-specific enclaves. According to Intel, TDX provides scalability, ease of deployment, and the operational model required for widespread adoption of confidential computing. Although SGX enabled confidential computing in the data center and continues to serve security-conscious customers, Intel believes future demand will favor TDX. Diamond Rapids will therefore be the final Xeon generation to support SGX, which gives customers several years to validate alternative solutions based on TDX and migrate existing applications. Intel will continue to provide security updates and support for SGX-enabled platforms into the early 2030s, so its customers will have plenty of time to adopt TDX for new deployments. You may like Hot Chips 2026: Intel Xeon 7 'Diamond Rapids' comes with up to 256 P-cores, 1.28 GB of last-level cache Intel layoffs to hit Data Center group Hot Chips 2026: Intel dives deep on Crescent Island AI accelerator Meanwhile, Intel plans to expand TDX capabilities with additional security technologies. These include Intel TDX Connect, which is designed to enable trusted I/O, as well as post-quantum cryptography and enhanced attestation mechanisms. Trusted I/O is particularly important for workloads that communicate with external devices, as protection of computations inside a virtual machine does not necessarily extend to data transferred between the VM and accelerators or other peripherals (read, CXL expanders, though Intel has not stated this for sure). Improved attestation will help organizations verify the integrity of protected environments, while post-quantum cryptography will help address future security threats. Meanwhile, Intel has not disclosed specific availability dates for these enhancements.One important driver behind Intel's confidential computing strategy seems to be accelerated adoption of agentic AI. Unlike conventional applications, autonomous agents may access sensitive enterprise information, execute operations across multiple systems, and interact with other agents. Intel expects many such workloads to run on CPUs, and here TDX may offer practical advantages for agentic AI applications. Unlike SGX, TDX can protect entire agent execution environments without extensive software modifications and enable multiple agents to operate in separate, hardware-isolated VMs on shared infrastructure. For GPU-accelerated AI workloads, Intel works with Nvidia to coordinate confidential computing technologies across CPUs and GPUs to extend protection to sensitive data and AI models throughout the processing pipeline (which is obviously broader than Intel's development of custom Xeon CPUs for Nvidia).Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsorsIntel TDX is already available through major cloud providers, including Alibaba Cloud, Google Cloud, IBM Cloud, Microsoft Azure, and Volcano Cloud. Meanwhile, Red Hat, Canonical, and VMware are adding TDX support to their software platforms to enable adoption in private clouds and enterprise environments. history.titleZh: Intel to phase out SGX after Xeon Diamond Rapids in favor of TDX
history.descriptionZh:
Intel于周五宣布，计划在即将推出的Xeon“Diamond Rapids”处理器之后停止对Software Guard Extensions（SGX）技术的支持，并将保密计算战略全面转向Trust Domain Extensions（TDX）。此时距离Intel将SGX引入主流服务器平台仅过去五年。Intel表示，现有支持SGX的平台将继续获得支持至2030年代初，同时会扩展TDX能力，以满足云计算、企业工作负载和代理式AI应用不断涌现的新需求。

背景方面，数据主权要求正成为越来越重要的因素。企业希望即使敏感信息在第三方运营的基础设施上处理，也能防止未经授权的访问。Intel SGX和TDX虽然都旨在保护使用中的数据，但技术路径差异显著。SGX在应用程序内部提供硬件保护的enclave，将选定代码和数据与操作系统、hypervisor等其他软件隔离。这需要开发者专门设计或修改应用来使用受保护enclave。TDX则隔离整个虚拟机，使其与底层宿主环境、hypervisor及其他虚拟机分离。TDX能够在不大量修改单个应用的情况下保护机密VM中的现有工作负载，这对运营大量虚拟机的云服务提供商尤其有吸引力。

尽管SGX和TDX多年来都面临过诸多安全漏洞，包括侧信道攻击、权限提升缺陷以及针对认证机制的攻击，但Intel并未将安全担忧列为停止SGX的原因。相反，Intel的决定反映了行业更偏好虚拟机级隔离，而非应用专用enclave。Intel认为，TDX具备大规模采用保密计算所需的可扩展性、易部署性和运营模式。SGX曾在数据中心实现保密计算，并继续服务于注重安全的客户，但未来需求将更倾向于TDX。因此，Diamond Rapids将成为最后一代支持SGX的Xeon，客户将有数年时间验证基于TDX的替代方案并迁移现有应用。

在扩展TDX方面，Intel计划加入额外安全技术，包括Intel TDX Connect、后量子密码学和增强认证机制。TDX Connect旨在实现可信I/O。对于需要与外部设备通信的工作负载，可信I/O尤为重要，因为虚拟机内部计算的保护并不一定自动延伸到VM与加速器或其他外设之间传输的数据，例如CXL扩展器，不过Intel尚未明确说明这一点。增强认证可帮助组织验证受保护环境的完整性，后量子密码学则用于应对未来安全威胁。Intel尚未公布这些增强功能的具体可用日期。

代理式AI的加速普及似乎是Intel保密计算战略的重要驱动力。与传统应用不同，自主代理可能访问敏感企业信息、跨多个系统执行操作，并与其他代理交互。Intel预计许多此类工作负载将在CPU上运行，而TDX可为代理式AI应用提供实际优势。与SGX不同，TDX无需大量软件修改即可保护整个代理执行环境，并允许多个代理在共享基础设施上以独立、硬件隔离的VM运行。对于GPU加速的AI工作负载，Intel与Nvidia合作协调CPU和GPU之间的保密计算技术，将保护扩展到整个处理管道中的敏感数据和AI模型。

生态方面，Intel TDX已通过主要云提供商提供，包括阿里云、谷歌云、IBM云、微软Azure和火山云。同时，Red Hat、Canonical和VMware正在其软件平台中增加TDX支持，以推动私有云和企业环境中的采用。

history.title: Diamond-infused watercooling coldplates for 2,300W Nvidia Rubin drop temps by up to 22C
history.description: A bespoke coldplate for custom designed AI servers: Frore's LiquidJet Diamond.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 4 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Frore Systems has introduced its bespoke LiquidJet Diamond liquid-cooling coldplate series that uses a diamond surface combined with a multi-stage 3D short-loop jet-channel microstructure to address precise hotspots on next-generation AI accelerators, such as AMD's Instinct MI400 and MI500-series, Nvidia's Rubin, and beyond. The company claims its new coldplates can handle hotspots with power densities reaching 770 W/cm², reduce GPU temperatures by up to 22C compared with conventional coldplates, and improve AI token throughput per watt by as much as 35%.LiquidJet Diamond combines the expertise it used for its original LiquidJet coldplate product and the LiquidJet Nexus bespoke coldplate for Nvidia Blackwell and Nvidia Rubin-based servers. Unlike Nexus, which integrates multiple coldplates into a large cooling assembly for several processors, LiquidJet Diamond is an individual GPU coldplate, albeit a bespoke one.From an internal technology perspective, Frore’s coldplates employ a three-dimensional, ultra-short-loop, multi-stage architecture with coolant channels customized for the power distribution of a specific processor. Meanwhile, the key innovation in LiquidJet Diamond is an additional heat spreader integrated into the bottom of the coldplate. This spreader incorporates diamond wafers positioned directly above the GPU’s hotspots to distribute heat more efficiently before it reaches the liquid-cooling structure. Diamond (carbon) has exceptionally high thermal conductivity, which can exceed 20 W/cm·K, compared with approximately 4 W/cm·K for copper. According to Frore, the addition of diamond heat spreaders allows LiquidJet Diamond to handle hotspots with power densities of up to 770 W/cm², compared with approximately 600 W/cm² for the original LiquidJet. However, the company has not disclosed how the diamond wafers are manufactured or integrated into the coldplate.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: According to Frore, its original LiquidJet coldplate reduces GPU temperatures by approximately 12C compared with conventional skived coldplates (based on its simulation model), which translates into a 25% improvement in AI tokens per watt, according to the company’s estimates. Meanwhile, a custom Liquid Diamond heatspreader promises to further reduce hotspot temperatures by up to 10°C, while the complete LiquidJet Diamond solution provides a 16C – 22C reduction in GPU temperatures and improves token efficiency by 30%–35%, Frore claims. The company also expects 75% higher heat-transfer efficiency and over 150% higher maximum hotspot power density than conventional cold plates based on its models.Frore plans to demonstrate LiquidJet Diamond at the OCP Global Summit on October 12 – 16, where it will showcase cooling for Nvidia's 2,300W Rubin accelerator and hotspots reaching 770 W/cm². However, the company has not disclosed whether the demonstration involves production GPUs or some type of thermal test vehicle. history.titleZh: Diamond-infused watercooling coldplates for 2,300W Nvidia Rubin drop temps by up to 22C
history.descriptionZh:
Frore Systems 发布了定制化 LiquidJet Diamond 液冷冷板系列，瞄准下一代 AI 加速器上越来越严峻的热点散热问题。该产品将金刚石表面/热扩散器与多级三维短回路射流通道微结构结合，目标平台包括 AMD Instinct MI400、MI500 系列，英伟达 Rubin 及后续产品。Frore 声称，新冷板可处理功率密度高达 770 W/cm² 的热点，使 GPU 温度较传统冷板最多降低 22°C，并将每瓦 AI token 吞吐量最多提升 35%。

背景上，LiquidJet Diamond 延续了 Frore 原有 LiquidJet 冷板以及面向英伟达 Blackwell 和 Rubin 服务器的定制 LiquidJet Nexus 冷板技术。Nexus 将多个冷板集成为大型冷却组件，用于服务多个处理器；LiquidJet Diamond 则是针对单个 GPU 的定制冷板。

核心技术原理方面，Frore 的冷板采用三维、超短回路、多级架构，冷却液通道会根据特定处理器的功率分布进行定制。LiquidJet Diamond 的关键创新是在冷板底部集成额外的热扩散器，其中金刚石晶圆直接布置在 GPU 热点上方，在热量进入液冷结构之前先更高效地扩散热量。金刚石（碳）具有极高导热率，可超过 20 W/cm·K，而铜约为 4 W/cm·K。据 Frore 介绍，加入金刚石热扩散器后，LiquidJet Diamond 可处理功率密度高达 770 W/cm² 的热点，而原始 LiquidJet 约为 600 W/cm²。不过，公司未披露金刚石晶圆如何制造或集成到冷板中。

性能对比方面，Frore 称，基于其仿真模型，原始 LiquidJet 冷板相比传统 skived 冷板可降低 GPU 温度约 12°C，相当于每瓦 AI token 提升约 25%。定制 Liquid Diamond 热扩散器有望进一步将热点温度最多降低 10°C；完整 LiquidJet Diamond 方案则可提供 16°C 至 22°C 的 GPU 降温，并将 token 效率提高 30% 至 35%。公司还预计，其传热效率比传统冷板高 75%，最大热点功率密度高 150% 以上。

应用与影响方面，该技术面向 AI 数据中心中功耗和热密度不断攀升的加速器，尤其是英伟达 Rubin 这类高功率平台。Frore 计划在 10 月 12 日至 16 日举行的 OCP Global Summit 上展示 LiquidJet Diamond，演示为英伟达 2300W Rubin 加速器散热以及应对 770 W/cm² 的热点。不过，公司尚未说明演示使用的是量产 GPU 还是某种热测试载体。若其宣称的性能能够实现，金刚石增强液冷冷板有望缓解下一代 AI 芯片的热瓶颈，提高液冷系统效率和 AI 计算能效。

history.title: AMD debuts Helion reference design for agentic AI servers with up to 32,768 Zen 6 ‘Venice’ cores
history.description: At the OCP Global Summit, AMD revealed Helion, a rack-scale reference design for agentic AI that can house up to 32,768 Zen 6 CPU cores.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 5 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Recent updates Updated 10/12/26 at 12:01pm ET: AMD originally said the Helion rack would ship in the first half of 2027, but it has revised the release date to November 2026. We've updated the headline and featured image. We also corrected an error where OpenU trays were marked as 21mm wide instead of 21 inches wide. AMD is bringing a new reference rack-scale design to the data center ecosystem with Helion. It’s a standardized, 21-inch rack reference design that will complement the Helios rack AMD revealed at OCP Global Summit last year. This year, we have Helion, which AMD says can house up to 32,768 Zen 6 cores in a CPU-only deployment using the dense 256-core design available with the EPYC ‘Venice’ 9996.Go deeper with TH Premium: CPU (Image credit: Tom's Hardware)Intel VP Robert Hallock sets Nova Lake expectations, teases return to Raptor Lake for DDR4 platformsCPU scaling with DLSSIntel's one-two punch plan in desktop CPUs is taking shapeBenchmarking AMD's BC-250, offering Steam Machine-like performance at half the priceAMD splits Zen 7 into three EPYC families for 2028 and starts selling server CPUs by the agent The rack design is standardized, based on the Open Compute Project’s ORv4 specification, which is slightly wider and taller than a standard IT rack. Helion is designed to support 44 OpenU trays, which are 21 inches wide and 48mm tall, slightly larger than a standard EA1-310 tray. AMD says the reference design supports both air-cooled and direct liquid-cooled deployments.The design is also compliant with OCP’s DC-MHS (Data Center Modular Hardware System) standard. MHS is designed to bring “interoperability between key elements of data center, edge, and enterprise infrastructure,” according to OCP.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Although AMD has renders of the design you can see in the presentation below, it won’t actually sell racks. This is a reference design that AMD is contributing to OCP, and OEMs and ODMs will actually bring that design to market. AMD didn’t share partners supporting Helion during a pre-briefing with the press. The company says CEO Lisa Su will announce partners during the lead keynote at the OCP Global Summit later today.AMD also didn’t share deployment partners, though it suggested that Helios customers will also deploy Helion racks. You may like AMD splits Zen 7 into three EPYC families for 2028 and starts selling server CPUs by the agent Microsoft will deploy AMD’s Helios rack-scale AI accelerator ‘at scale’ on Azure AMD takes the wraps off its Instinct MI455X AI accelerator Unlike Helios, which is built for AI training and inference, Helion is a more flexible rack solution primarily focused on CPUs. In a CPU-only deployment, the design can hold up to 128 EPYC 9996 CPUs, bringing that impressive 32,768 core count per rack. This configuration would likely look something like an agentic AI sandbox system, which is then connected to an inference system.This model for personal AI agents is in use today, both in Meta’s Muse and OpenAI Dots. Each user has a sandbox with a slice of compute from the host system, with the backbone of an inference server. Some workloads are handled on those CPU-only servers, such as building software, but the heavy-duty AI inference happens elsewhere.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsorsPresumably, this is the model AMD is aiming at with Helion as hyperscalers build out CPU capacity on the back of agentic AI. history.titleZh: AMD推出Helion参考设计，用于代理式AI服务器，最高支持32,768个Zen 6“Venice”核心
history.descriptionZh:
AMD在OCP全球峰会上推出面向数据中心生态的新机架级参考设计Helion，用于补充去年发布的Helios机架。Helion是标准化21英寸机架参考设计，基于开放计算项目（OCP）的ORv4规范，比标准IT机架略宽略高，支持44个OpenU托盘，每个托盘宽21英寸、高48毫米，略大于标准EA1-310托盘。它兼容OCP的DC-MHS（数据中心模块化硬件系统）标准，目标是提升数据中心、边缘和企业基础设施关键组件之间的互操作性，并同时支持风冷和直接液冷部署。

核心配置上，Helion在纯CPU部署中最高可容纳128颗AMD EPYC 9996“Venice”处理器，借助其256核设计，单机架可达32768个Zen 6核心。AMD认为这种配置适合代理式AI（agentic AI）沙箱系统，并与推理系统相连。类似模式已在Meta Muse和OpenAI Dots中使用：每个用户获得主机系统切分出的部分计算资源作为沙箱，推理服务器作为骨干；软件构建等部分负载由纯CPU服务器处理，重型AI推理则在其他系统完成。随着超大规模云厂商因代理式AI扩大CPU容量，这可能是Helion瞄准的场景。

与Helios主要面向AI训练和推理不同，Helion更灵活，主要聚焦CPU，但也可混合配置：最多支持16块MI350P GPU和102 Tbps网络，代价是减少CPU容量。AMD称这种混合配置面向企业，可提供集数据管理、网络和AI使用于一体的一体化机架。

商业模式上，AMD不会直接销售Helion机架，而是将其作为参考设计贡献给OCP，由OEM和ODM推向市场。AMD在预简报中未公布支持Helion的合作伙伴，称CEO苏姿丰将在OCP Global Summit主keynote上宣布；也未公布部署合作伙伴，但暗示Helios客户也会部署Helion机架。

发布时间方面，文章更新称，AMD原计划Helion机架于2027年上半年出货，后修订为2026年11月。更新还更正了OpenU托盘宽度应为21英寸而非21毫米。原文底部仍写“2027年上半年”，可能未同步更新。整体来看，Helion是AMD围绕Zen 6 EPYC和代理式AI基础设施，向开放计算生态提交的高密度、可扩展CPU/混合机架蓝图。

Maia 300 not only improves the cost and efficiency of running AI workloads in the cloud, it’s also more capable of handling the latest reasoning models and agentic tasks.Maia 300 will start being rolled out to production in 2027, and it has been designed with efficiency in mind. “We expect Maia 300 to deliver 40 percent more tokens per megawatt compared to leading GPU-based systems,” says Scott Guthrie, executive vice president of Microsoft’s cloud group. “And in a full 96-accelerator configuration, it delivers up to 7x the rack-scale token throughput of Maia 200.”These efficiency improvements will allow Microsoft to rely mainly on its in-house AI chips soon, instead of ones from Nvidia and AMD. “We will scale our Azure Maia family to multi-gigawatt deployments starting in 2027, making Maia the primary AI inference system for Microsoft products and services,” says Guthrie.Maia 300 chips will start being used for production workloads in 2027. Image: MicrosoftMaia 300 is a successor to the 200, which was only announced in January. Maia 200 is already running on production AI workloads across Microsoft, including Microsoft Copilot, GitHub Copilot, Microsoft Foundry, and Microsoft’s own AI models.“Maia 200 is the best performing AI infrastructure in our fleet, measured in real world metrics for AI services,” says Guthrie. “Maia 300 is a complete AI system designed for the new types of AI workloads emerging today: Long-context reasoning, latency-sensitive conversational experiences, and sustained, multi-step agentic tasks.”RelatedMicrosoft is finally making custom chips — and they’re all about AIMicrosoft’s latest AI chip goes head-to-head with Amazon and GoogleMicrosoft is using a new chiplet architecture to get its all-important efficiency gains. Built on TSMC’s N2P process node, the latest Maia 300 architecture separates compute, memory controller, and I/O functions. “This increases the silicon area dedicated to compute performance and allows each function to use the technology best suited to its role,” says the Azure hardware and infrastructure team.Maia 300 is also a key part of Microsoft’s own AI model work, and could help the company achieve its goal of catching up with Google DeepMind, OpenAI, and Anthropic. “We have to work across the full stack, all the way down to the silicon,” says Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman. “At that scale we need a platform that we own, and that we co-design with our models. That’s why running our Microsoft AI models on top of the Maia chip is a critical focus for our team.”

history.title: Buyer pays $350 for broken RTX 4090 project only to find realistic fake GPU die and swapped memory
history.description: A customer paid approximately $350 for what appeared to be a repairable RTX 4090, only to receive a fake GPU with components that were painstakingly designed to resemble the real thing.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter A GPU repair specialist has uncovered another GPU scam involving a counterfeit RTX 4090, with a fake GPU die and memory chips designed to resemble genuine components. The graphics card was purchased for 30,000 Rubles, or approximately $350, as a potential repair project. However, upon close inspection, it was revealed that the board was fitted with dummy components.According to VIK-off (h/t VideoCardz), the Russian repair specialist received the GPU from a customer who purchased the card as a bare printed circuit board (PCB). Since the original cooling system was missing, it was difficult to verify whether it actually worked before the purchase was made. Now we’ve seen similar scams in the past, but this particular case stands out due to the sheer effort that was put into making the counterfeit components.According to Vik-Off, the counterfeiters managed to replicate intricate details including the labeling, GPU package, chip markings, as well as the compound surrounding the processor. The fake GPU die was even soldered onto the PCB using a ball grid array (BGA), making it appear as though it had been installed during the original manufacturing process.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: However, certain inconsistencies gave it away, like the color of the substrate, surface reflections, and certain lettering. After removing the fake GPU package, the repair specialist found that its contact area did not resemble that of a functional processor, while the solder mask started to deteriorate during cleaning. (Image credit: Videocardz)Even though the memory chips looked genuine at first, removing one of the packages revealed what appeared to be GDDR6 memory rather than the GDDR6X chips used on the RTX 4090. The markings on these chips closely resembled genuine Micron memory packages, making the counterfeits even more difficult to identify. Vik-Off suspects the PCB design could be based on an RTX 3090 Ti, although there is no conclusive proof. You may like German scammer dupes two different buyers into spending thousands on hollow RTX 5090 GPUs Japanese repair shop sells GPU VRAM upgrades for $25 per GB during memory crisis Techno-bandits secretly swap RTX 5080 GPUs with RTX 3080s in Chinese esports hotel This isn’t the first time a counterfeit RTX 4090 has made its way into the hands of customers. Back in June, Chinese hardware shop owner Brother Zhang came across a broken RTX 4090 that had been purchased for around $222. A closer inspection revealed that the card was essentially a replica with a plastic imitation of Nvidia’s AD102 GPU die instead of the actual silicon. Additionally, the "TW 3043E2" marking indicated that the card was somehow manufactured in 2030.One should always be cautious when purchasing used high-end graphics cards, especially those marked as repairable or untested. The onboard components and chip markings might look convincing, but that does not guarantee that the hardware inside is genuine. history.titleZh: 买家花350美元买下损坏的RTX 4090项目卡，却发现是逼真的假GPU核心和调换过的显存
history.descriptionZh:
俄罗斯GPU维修专家VIK-off披露，一宗针对二手市场的假冒RTX 4090骗局被识破。客户以3万卢布、约350美元购买了一块只有裸PCB的“RTX 4090”，因原装散热器缺失，交易前无法验证是否能点亮，原本打算作为维修项目。VIK-off检查后发现，板上GPU核心与显存均为假件。与以往粗糙仿品不同，造假者复制了标签、GPU封装、芯片丝印以及核心周围填充胶等细节，甚至用BGA焊球将假GPU die焊在PCB上，使其看起来像原厂安装。但基板颜色、表面反光、字体等露出破绽。拆下假GPU封装后，接触区域不像正常处理器，清洁时阻焊层也开始脱落。

显存方面，假芯片外观和丝印高度模仿正品美光颗粒，拆开一个封装后发现实际是GDDR6，而非RTX 4090应有的GDDR6X。Vik-Off怀疑该PCB设计可能基于RTX 3090 Ti，但尚无确凿证据。由于核心和显存均为假件，这块卡不可能具备RTX 4090的性能，也无法正常用于游戏、渲染或AI计算。RTX 4090作为高端显卡，本应配备GDDR6X显存和完整AD102核心，而假卡从芯片层级就不具备对应功能。

类似案件并非孤例。今年6月中国硬件店主Brother Zhang曾遇到一块约222美元购入的故障RTX 4090，检查发现它用塑料冒充Nvidia AD102 GPU核心，且“TW 3043E2”标记竟显示2030年制造。文章提醒，购买二手高端显卡尤其标注“可维修”“未测试”的产品需格外谨慎；元件和芯片丝印可能逼真，但不代表硬件真实。应要求卖家证明显卡可工作，并尽可能装入系统实测后再付款。

此案的技术影响在于，GPU造假已从简单换壳、贴假标签升级到封装级、BGA焊接级伪装，增加了维修人员和买家的识别难度。对二手交易、维修回收以及依赖高端GPU的AI、游戏和内容创作市场而言，检测需综合检查基板、封装、阻焊层、显存类型、BGA焊点和上机测试，单看外观已不足以防骗。
